latest_release.name: 🍂🐮 Moovember 2026 | Feature & Security Update: Mailbox Groups, imapsync Rework & SOGo 5.12.13
latest_release.body:
> [!CAUTION]
> **Please create a backup before updating.**

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Important security update. We strongly recommend updating as soon as possible.**
> Among other issues, this release fixes a remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability that can be exploited by authenticated admins and domain admins.
> Details on the fixed issues will be published early next week. Please read the breaking changes before updating.
> **Workaround** until you can update: limit access to admin and domain admin accounts.



## ⚠️ Breaking Changes
- **Sync job API**: `add/syncjob` needs a `source_id`, and the server fields (`host1`, `port1`, `enc1`, `authmech1`) are no longer accepted or returned. Existing jobs are migrated automatically.
  **Action:** If you create or read sync jobs through the API, update your client. Create a source with `add/syncjob_source` (or look it up with `get/syncjob_source/all`) and pass its `source_id`.
- **Request body limit**: 64 MB for UI/API, `NGINX_MAX_BODY_SIZE` (default `128m`) for SOGo/EAS/DAV. If it is below your Postfix `message_size_limit`, large mails can't be sent via SOGo webmail or ActiveSync.
  **Action:** If you raised the Postfix message size limit, set `NGINX_MAX_BODY_SIZE` in `mailcow.conf` above it and run `docker compose up -d`.
- **Custom nginx locations** (`data/conf/nginx/site.*.custom`): they are now limited to 64 MB as well, before there was no limit. Apps you run under the mailcow host this way (e.g. Nextcloud or Gitea under a path) reject larger uploads with `413`. Own server blocks in `data/conf/nginx/*.conf` (e.g. Nextcloud on its own subdomain) are not affected.
  **Action:** Add `client_max_body_size` to your location (e.g. `client_max_body_size 0;` for no limit) and run `docker compose restart nginx-mailcow`.

## 🔐 Security
- SOGo 5.12.13, an upstream security release ([notes](https://github.com/Alinto/sogo/releases/tag/SOGo-5.12.13))
- Several security fixes in mailcow (details next week)
- Fail2ban counts failed logins of all protocols (IMAP, POP3, SMTP, Sieve, EAS, DAV), 2FA rate limit

## 🚀 New Features

All new features are documented at https://docs.mailcow.email/.

### Mailbox groups & shared mailboxes
- Groups with their own address work as distribution lists. Members can come from all domains you manage.
- Members can send as the group address and as other addresses of the group.
- Share mailboxes with a group (IMAP, shown as `Shared/<mailbox>`), as well as SOGo calendars and address books. Members can be subscribed automatically.
- Shared mailboxes have no login of their own and are accessed through groups.
- Mailbox templates can be assigned per group, with a priority.
- Domain admins manage the groups of their domains (new ACL "Mailbox groups").

### Identity provider sync (Keycloak, LDAP/AD)
- Groups from the IdP are synced to mailcow groups, including their members.
- Optional offboarding: if a user is disabled or deleted in the IdP, the mailbox login is disabled, but mail is still delivered. Off by default.
- The admin UI shows the sync status, conflicts and a preview.

### imapsync rework
- **Sync sources**: the server settings (host, port, encryption, authentication) are defined once and used by any number of jobs. A source can be available to everyone, to specific domains or to single users. Presets cover common providers.
- **OAuth2 (XOAUTH2)** for Microsoft 365 and Google. Tokens are refreshed automatically, even while a job is running.
- **Parallel jobs**: several jobs run at the same time. The maximum and a bandwidth limit can be set in the admin UI.
- The certificate of the source server is verified (SSL and STARTTLS). The check can be turned off per source.
- Updated to imapsync 2.314.

### API keys
- Any number of API keys, each with a description, read-only or read-write access and its own IP allowlist.
- Keys from `mailcow.conf` are shown as locked service keys.
